claims.value: Foy gives side A 8,000 crossing the Tagus under Loison for the Évora expedition.
claims.rationale: Expedition departure population, not an exact 29 July engaged return. English rendering (ours): "Accordingly Loison crossed the Tagus on 25 July at the head of 8,000 men."

citations.locator: foy-t4, printed p. 265, Internet Archive leaf 274; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: En conséquence, Loison passa le Tage le 25 juillet, à la tête de huit mille hommes.

claims.value: Foy gives side B 5,000 organized Portuguese/Spanish troops, excluding the irregular mass arriving to fight.
claims.rationale: French-mediated opponent estimate; no separately inspected Portuguese return. Civilians are not added as a guessed remainder. English rendering (ours): "Together with those already in Évora, Portuguese and Spaniards made 5,000, excluding the disorganized mass who came to fight outside the regular corps."

citations.locator: foy-t4, printed p. 268, Internet Archive leaf 277; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Elles formaient entre Portugais et Espagnols, avec ce qui était déjà à Evora, une force de cinq mille hommes, non compris la masse désordonnée de ceux qui étaient venus pour combattre, quoique ne faisant pas partie des corps réguliers.

claims.value: Foy names Leite and Moretti directing side B’s deployment, and Solignac and Margaron under Loison.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Portuguese General Leite and Spanish Colonel Moretti arrayed their small army; two French brigades were under Generals Solignac and Margaron."

claims.value: Loison ordered Solignac to turn the defending flank and go around the south of Évora.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "He sent his first brigade right, ordering Solignac to outflank the enemy and go around the city to the south."

claims.value: Side B had a neglected bastioned enceinte; principal breaches were hastily retrenched.
claims.rationale: The permanent enceinte is inherited; no assignment of the repairs to a named engagement commander. English rendering (ours): "The enceinte had not been maintained since the old Spanish wars; parapets had disappeared and masonry fallen. The main breaches were cleared and hastily retrenched."

claims.value: Oman gives the organized Portuguese and Spanish allies under 3,000, with armed peasants and citizens separately manning the town walls.
claims.rationale: The same paragraph separates the organized field line from the mixed crowd on the walls. The footnote transmits the Portuguese historian Neves through Arteche; neither was separately inspected. Alternative to Foy’s 5,000, not a new Portuguese original return.

open_questions: Establish the Portuguese and Spanish organized troops separately from armed townspeople through Leite/Moretti returns or Portuguese histories.
Deferred: the dated original returns and reports identified above, and any deeper source-lineage reconciliation. No additional research cycle follows merely from this gap.

Source dependence: Bodart is a later compilation. Toreno, Foy, Oman, Saint-Cyr and the official Correspondance are interested or retrospective source families, and embedded/reprinted reports are not extra independent witnesses. Agreement does not establish independence.

A.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Source-specific alternatives below retain their own moment and population. Alternatives/limits: Foy gives side A 8,000 crossing the Tagus under Loison for the Évora expedition.
A.command_scope: Printed side-A commander Loison; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Foy names Leite and Moretti directing side B’s deployment, and Solignac and Margaron under Loison.
A.army_continuity: Unknown: these passages do not establish a cross-engagement army identity.

B.strength_population_and_time: Bodart’s engagement-level available force; no dated opening return. Civilians, recruits, regular troops and surrender survivors are not interchangeable. Alternatives/limits: Foy gives side B 5,000 organized Portuguese/Spanish troops, excluding the irregular mass arriving to fight. Oman’s mediated Neves/Arteche account gives under 3,000 organized allies, separating the wall crowd; source disagreement is unresolved.
B.command_scope: Printed side-B commander Leite; local/superior authority and transitions remain limited to the additional passages cited below. Foy names Leite and Moretti directing side B’s deployment, and Solignac and Margaron under Loison.
B.army_continuity: Unknown: repeated names and formation labels do not establish continuity.

research_completion.stopping_reason: The per-side strength/command checklist and nine dimensions are covered by supported observations or explicit unknowns. The remaining decision-relevant gap is deferred; no feature admission follows.
